cards.explanation: The answer is those who work hard among them. The writers ask the brothers to "…acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who care for you in the Lord and who admonish you." (1 Thessalonians 5:12) That's three jobs in one sentence: working hard, caring and admonishing. The letter says to notice the people doing them, friends.

The answer is "encourage." The verse says to "…admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone." (1 Thessalonians 5:14) Four kinds of care, and each one fits a different need. A nervous heart gets a hand on the shoulder, not a lecture, friends.

The answer is False. The letter says "…be patient with everyone." and everyone means everyone. (1 Thessalonians 5:14) There's no insider-only section in that sentence. Just a short, big command, and I'm still working on it myself.

The answer is that no one repays evil for evil. The letter says, "Make sure that no one repays evil for evil." (1 Thessalonians 5:15) Notice it says no one, so it's a job for the whole group. Put the phone down, friends, and leave that reply unsent.

The answer is always rejoice and never stop praying. "Rejoice at all times. Pray without ceasing." (1 Thessalonians 5:16-17) At all times and without ceasing. No days off from either one. I'll be honest, I can barely go a whole afternoon without checking the timer, and the letter says never stop.

The answer is True. The letter says, "Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus." (1 Thessalonians 5:18) Every circumstance, and the letter says this is God's will for them in Christ Jesus. That's a big one, so give thanks even when the batch comes out flat, friends.

The answer is to test all things. "Do not treat prophecies with contempt, but test all things. Hold fast to what is good." (1 Thessalonians 5:20-21) No sneering at prophecies, and no swallowing everything whole either. You test, and then you hold on to the good, friends.

The answer is "evil." The letter says, "Abstain from every form of evil." (1 Thessalonians 5:22) Just before it comes "…test all things. Hold fast to what is good." (1 Thessalonians 5:21) So good gets the grip, and evil gets the cold shoulder. Every form means every form, not just the big ones.

The answer is False. It isn't only the soul. The letter says, "…may your entire spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ." (1 Thessalonians 5:23) The whole person is covered, and that's good news for every one of us, friends.

The answer is the One who calls them. The letter says, "The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it." (1 Thessalonians 5:24) The "it" is the sanctifying and keeping blameless from the verse before. The letter puts that big job on the One who calls. That's a relief, friends, because I couldn't carry that batch myself.

The answer is True. The writer says, "I charge you before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers." (1 Thessalonians 5:27) Charged before the Lord, so it's no small request. The letter is meant to be read to all the brothers, friends.
